title: Release Tracks, Staged Rollout, and Rollback Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies release tracks, staged rollout, and rollback?
options: Promote incrementally using predefined health evidence and rehearsed version-compatible recovery.
Assume Play can always downgrade users
Ship a breaking backend change before adoption
questions.answer: Promote incrementally using predefined health evidence and rehearsed version-compatible recovery.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: Stopping a staged rollout automatically downgrades users who already received the release.
questions.explanation: A staged rollout cannot protect users when a backward-incompatible server or database change affects all installed versions immediately.

questions.prompt: Why must backend contracts tolerate overlapping app versions?
questions.answer: Staged rollout and rollback leave several client versions active concurrently.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
